name: Heat + new competitor
description: The heat spell Austin actually had - 21-22 July, 4.6C above the 30-year normal for those dates - and a new coffee bar opening 380m up the block on 20 July. Tickets fall but basket size RISES: fewer people, buying iced drinks, later in the day. Two drivers pulling opposite ways on one series, separable only because the competitor is still there after the heat breaks.
expectation: Two things should happen, and the second is the point. The competitor should be identified (~-5 pts) because it is still there after the heat breaks - days when only one driver is active are the only days that identify either. The HEAT should come out UNPROVEN: two days is almost no statistical power, so its band crosses zero and the engine says it may have done nothing. That is the correct answer, not a shortfall. A scenario named after a heat wave whose heat the engine refuses to claim is the clearest demonstration in the demo that it does not over-read thin evidence.

meta.note: Persists after the heat breaks. That persistence is the only thing that identifies it separately from the heat, which is why the window extends well past the hot days.
